item.title: Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABNT20 KNHC 281736
TWOAT

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 PM EDT Mon Sep 28 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Depression Fay, located well to the west-southwest of the Azores and
on newly formed Tropical Storm Hanna, located well to the
east-northeast of Bermuda.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected over the next 7 days.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Storm Hanna are issued under WMO
header WTNT33 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPAT3.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Hanna are issued under WMO
header WTNT23 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMAT3.

$$
Forecaster Papin

...FAY HOLDING STEADY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 PM AST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...26.6N 45.3W
ABOUT 1325 MI...2130 KM WSW OF THE AZORES
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...SW OR 220 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1011 MB...29.86 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 PM AST (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression Fay was 
located near latitude 26.6 North, longitude 45.3 West. The 
depression is moving toward the southwest near 9 mph (15 km/h). A 
southwest to west-southwest motion, along with an increase in 
forward speed, is expected over the next couple of days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts. 
Little change in strength is forecast during the next day or so, and 
Fay is forecast to become a post-tropical cyclone in 36 h.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1011 mb (29.86 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 PM AST.
 
$$
Forecaster Kelly

item.title: Tropical Depression Fay Forecast Discussion Number 35
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM AST Mon Sep 28 2026 
861 
WTNT41 KNHC 282032
TCDAT1
 
Tropical Depression Fay Discussion Number  35
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
500 PM AST Mon Sep 28 2026
 
Fay has continued to produce bursts of deep convection this 
afternoon, primarily sheared to the south of the low-level center. 
The overall satellite presentation has improved slightly since 
earlier today, featuring cold cloud tops near -70C. Objective 
UW-CIMSS satellite intensity estimates have been running slightly 
higher than the scatterometer-derived surface wind data from earlier 
today. However, the subjective Dvorak intensity estimate from TAFB 
has held steady at T2.0/30 kt. Accordingly, the initial intensity is 
maintained at 30 kt for this advisory.
 
The depression is moving southwestward with an estimated initial 
motion of 220/8 kt. A general southwest to west-southwest motion is 
anticipated over the next couple of days as Fay is steered by the 
flow along the southern periphery of a mid-level ridge situated over 
the central Atlantic. The latest NHC track forecast is essentially 
an update of the previous advisory and lies very close to the HCCA 
corrected-consensus aid.
 
Fay continues to defy model guidance by maintaining deep convection 
near its low-level center. Given that vertical wind shear remains 
low-to-moderate and sea surface temperatures are near 29C, it is 
entirely possible that Fay could briefly regain tropical storm 
strength tonight. Global models persist in showing that the system 
will struggle to sustain deep convection in a day or so as it 
encounters a more stable air mass and upper-level convergence. 
Nevertheless, Fay has proven to be a resilient, small system. The 
latest NHC intensity forecast holds Fay steady through Tuesday 
followed by gradual weakening, with the system forecast to become a 
post-tropical cyclone in a day or so, and degenerate into a remnant 
trough in a couple of days.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS

item.title: Tropical Storm Hanna Forecast Discussion Number 1
item.description:
Issued at 1100 AM AST Mon Sep 28 2026 
000
WTNT43 KNHC 281500
TCDAT3
 
Tropical Storm Hanna Discussion Number   1
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL082026
1100 AM AST Mon Sep 28 2026
 
Recent scatterometer data shows that the disturbance that NHC has 
been tracking over the central subtropical Atlantic has acquired a 
well-defined surface circulation and center.  Despite significant 
westerly shear the system has maintained an area of deep convection 
to the east of the center, and the scatterometer data revealed peak 
winds of 35 to 40 kt to the southeast of the center.  As a result 
of this data, the system is being upgraded to 40-kt tropical 
storm Hanna at this time.  

The shear over the tropical storm is expected to remain strong out 
of the west-northwest for the next several days, so little, if any, 
strengthening is anticipated.  In a couple of days, the shear and 
dry mid-level air are likely to cause weakening.  Simulated 
satellite imagery from the global models indicated the deep 
convection is likely to cease in about 60 hours, therefore the NHC 
forecast calls for it to become a remnant low at that time. 

Hanna is moving eastward at about 15 kt.  An eastward to 
east-southeastward motion is forecast during the next 24 hours as 
the system is embedded along the southern side of the mid-latitude 
westerlies. After that time, the westerlies lift northward and the 
steering flow will weaken, causing the system to slow down and turn 
east-northeastward. The NHC track forecast is close to the HCCA and 
GDMI models which are along the southern side of the model envelope.
